calendar.impact: An energy ceasefire is on Ukraine's agenda for the fourth US-mediated round, going in against the heaviest combined strike week of the autumn: 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones on Ukraine's grid overnight Nov 6-7, six Russian refineries struck since Oct 30 with Yanos halted and Saratov hit.
calendar.title: US-hosted Ukraine and Russia talks, Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11)

calendar.impact: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 6 is released a day late for Veterans Day, at 12:00 p.m. ET. It is the first balance print after the repricing, and distillate at 99.3 million barrels is the line that matters.
calendar.title: EIA weekly petroleum report, 12:00 p.m. ET (delayed for Veterans Day)

calendar.impact: The deadline for December shipper nominations. The registered December judgment call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows the close.
calendar.title: December Mainline nominations close

calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the fourth quarter capacity review setting the baselines for 2027 quotas.
calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework

changes.balance: Saturday paired the two branches in one evening: the blockade fired on a named vessel, and the mediators published their most concrete terms yet, a day-two Hormuz reopening against nuclear inspections with part of $8 billion in frozen assets released. The confirmed barrel count did not change, the disabled ship carried no crude and the claimed tankers are unconfirmed, but the enforcement regime's demonstrated willingness to fire prices through transit behaviour, freight and insurance before it prices through supply.
changes.body: US Central Command said US forces disabled the St. Kitts-flagged bulk carrier M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman on Nov 7, firing precision munitions at its stern after the crew ignored repeated warnings and tried several times to break the naval blockade after calling at an Iranian port; CENTCOM's tally since July is 147 vessels redirected and five merchant ships disabled. Twenty-one minutes later the IRGC announced two oil tankers had struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz; no vessel is named and no independent source has confirmed either tanker. The UAE National Guard rescued 22 crew from a cargo ship fire in the Sea of Oman, vessel unnamed and cause unstated. The Qatari proposal reported Nov 7 would lift the blockade and release part of about $8 billion in frozen assets against IAEA inspections of Iran's bombed nuclear sites, with the strait reopening on day two through the route negotiated with Oman; Tehran's stated obstacles are its seven conditions and distrust of the IAEA director general, and Qatar rejected reports the mediation had collapsed. Friday's settles stand: Brent Jan27 $98.32 and WTI Dec26 $90.83 (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 6). December WCS is -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6) on zero lots. The validated diesel crack is $91.10.
changes.conditional: A published acceptance of the Qatari proposal, a confirmed tanker loss, or Monday's settle would each regrade the weekend; a Monday fade toward $93 to $94 tests the week's floor a third time.
changes.delta: CENTCOM (Nov 7): M/V Huda disabled in the Gulf of Oman, precision munitions at the stern, 147 vessels redirected and five merchant ships disabled since July. IRGC (Nov 7, 20:56 GMT): two tankers claimed on mines, unnamed, unconfirmed. UAE National Guard (Nov 8): 22 crew rescued from a cargo ship fire in the Sea of Oman, all stable. Qatari proposal (reported Nov 7): blockade lifted and part of $8 billion released against IAEA inspections, strait reopening day two via the Oman route. Friday settles: Brent Jan27 $98.32, WTI Dec26 $90.83. December WCS -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6) on zero lots.
changes.source: US Central Command, Nov 7, 2026; Xinhua and TASS, Nov 7-8, 2026; UAE National Guard via WAM, Nov 8, 2026; The Guardian, Nov 7, 2026; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 6, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 6, 2026
changes.title: The blockade fired on a named vessel Saturday evening, the IRGC claimed two tankers on mines minutes later, and Qatar's proposal would reopen Hormuz on day two

changes.balance: December stays a space and freight price with the operator's own confirmation behind the space leg, and the front month itself still has not traded tighter, so the healing evidence remains entirely in the deferred tenors and in Houston. Nothing in the Canadian market trades again until Monday.
changes.body: December WCS is -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6) on zero lots, a second straight zero-lot tightening in Friday's file, so the move is a mark, not a traded settle. The traded strip tightened for a third straight session on Friday: Jan27 -$23.85 on 1 lot, Feb27 -$23.30 on 55 lots, Apr27 -$19.35 on 275 lots, May27 -$18.30 on 275 lots and Jun27 -$17.10 on 275 lots, with Jul27 through Sep27 each on 435 lots. Houston tightened more on heavier volume: Jan27 -$16.35 on 725 lots, Feb27 -$14.90 on 685, Mar27 -$13.45 on 685, Apr27 -$12.10 on 745, May27 -$10.70 on 745, Jun27 -$9.30 on 745, and Jul27 through Sep27 flat at -$9.25 on 360 lots each. The December export spread stands at +$10.73 because both December legs are marks and Houston's mark moved further; January's spread is +$7.50.
changes.conditional: A December settle tighter on traded volume would be the first traded confirmation that the front is healing; the December apportionment notice after the Nov 17 nominations close settles the space leg against the registered call.
changes.delta: December WCS -$29.67 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 6), marked $0.48 tighter on zero lots, second straight zero-lot tightening. Houston Jan27 -$16.35 on 725 lots; Apr27 to Jun27 on 745 lots each. December ARV to TMW spread +$10.73, January +$7.50. No weekend trading; Friday's file is the latest.
changes.title: December WCS stands as a zero-lot mark into Monday while the traded deferred strip and Houston carry the tightening

changes.balance: Saturday's fuller accounting makes the Abu Dhabi round the week's hinge: Russia's heaviest grid barrage of the autumn and Ukraine's six-plant refinery campaign both landed in the same week the talks convene, so any energy ceasefire language moves products and differentials first and flat price second.
changes.body: The overnight Nov 6-7 Russian barrage, reported in full on Saturday, was 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones across 12 regions, with four ballistic missiles intercepted on Ukraine's account; substations carrying power from the Rivne and Khmelnytsky nuclear plants to Kyiv and central regions were damaged, power was cut in five regions, Kyiv's Northern Bridge closed, and a Naftogaz oil and gas facility in central Ukraine was hit three times with a major fire and no employee injuries. At least two people were killed and about a dozen wounded. On Saratov, the governor reported injuries and residential damage, monitoring analysts geolocated a refinery fire from eyewitness video, and Russian authorities have not officially confirmed a refinery fire or disclosed damage. Ukraine's campaign stands at six plants struck since Oct 30 with Yanos halted.
changes.conditional: Energy ceasefire language out of Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11 regrades the products leg; a further strike round during the talks extends the campaign frame.
changes.delta: Ukraine energy ministry and Naftogaz (Nov 7): 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones overnight Nov 6-7, nuclear-plant transmission substations damaged, power cut in five regions, Northern Bridge closed, Naftogaz facility hit three times. Saratov: governor reported injuries; refinery fire geolocated by monitoring analysts; no official Russian confirmation of a refinery fire.
changes.source: Ukraine energy ministry and Naftogaz, Nov 7, 2026; Saratov regional governor and ASTRA reporting, Nov 7, 2026
changes.title: Saturday's accounting of the Nov 6-7 barrage: 36 ballistic missiles on the grid, nuclear-plant substations damaged, Saratov damage still unassessed

flags.body: The blockade fired on a named vessel on Nov 7: CENTCOM disabled the M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman, its fifth merchant ship disabled since July on its own count, with 147 redirected. The IRGC claimed two tankers on mines twenty-one minutes later, unnamed and unconfirmed. The Qatari proposal reported the same day would lift the blockade and release part of $8 billion in frozen assets against IAEA inspections, with the strait reopening on day two; Tehran's seven conditions and its distrust of the IAEA director general are the stated obstacles, and Qatar rejected collapse reports. Eurasia Group (Nov 5) prices renewed strikes at 60 percent with a $110 to $125 Brent band, a deal at 10 percent and a standoff at 30 percent; that frame predates both Saturday events. The new Congress is seated Jan 3, 2027; until then the administration's foreign policy runs under the existing composition.
flags.title: Blockade enforcement went kinetic and the deal shape went public on the same evening: both branches now carry evidence
flags.trigger: A published agreement or acceptance in the mediator process, a confirmed tanker loss or further enforcement action, Monday's settle, or the Abu Dhabi talks on Nov 10-11

flags.body: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. The registered December judgment call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack now includes six wide or marked December settlements, a deferred strip that has tightened on traded volume for three straight sessions with Houston leading, and the operator's own statement on Nov 6 that the Mainline is at or near capacity and expected to remain in apportionment for the foreseeable future. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows the close and grades the call.
flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, the operator says apportionment persists, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop before the nominations close

flags.body: Distillate stocks are 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003 and 13 percent below the five-year average, after a 3.565 million barrel draw in the week ending Oct 30. The validated diesel crack is $91.10, and Ukraine's refinery campaign, six plants struck since Oct 30 with Yanos halted and Saratov hit overnight into Nov 7, keeps Atlantic basin product supply under pressure while Russian product exports stay restricted. The first Russian diesel cargo under the US arrangement had a listed Nov 7 arrival at New York and New Jersey with no discharge confirmed at run time. The next inventory report is Thursday Nov 12.
flags.title: Distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003: the products leg is the tight part of the US balance into winter
flags.trigger: The EIA release at 12:00 p.m. ET on Nov 12, a distillate stock build back above 105 million barrels, or a diesel crack break in either direction
